items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: My bass player, one of my steady bass players, Boots Malison... I also played as well. That took some doing... And I had James Chirillo on guitar and Boots Malison on bass

ctx.x: So if you’re accompanying a singer, unless you really know this song, you don’t know what pitches they’re singing and I find that really sort of false.

Well don’t get me started on this whole century. Because I’m glad I’m here, I make the best of it, I try, you know I try to get into the advanced things but I really don’t get it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Although I do appreciate the technology and I appreciate the skill that it takes to manipulate it and what they can do, but I am on the fence. I am seeing more and more people even my age using them. My bass player, one of my steady bass players, Boots Malison, a wonderful, wonderful musician, says that some of his, he calls them “accounts” some of his accounts hand out not music, they hand out an iPad just for this musician for the show. I mean like five iPads they bring to the gig. But I remember — this sticks…

ctx.x: Chaucer. Chaucer. But he also was not playing “Lady of Spain” he was one of the first to get those — all those new-fangled things that the accordions were able to do — yeah, like a computer. Almost like an electric piano. So he had one of those and he wasn’t a jazz player but he could play really good harmony on the accordion and that’s what I got used to, singing. And later on my father encouraged me to accompany myself and sing with myself. So I had both.
Do you think you accompany significantly differently when you accompany another singer?
